title: BottomTabBar
summary: Three to five top-level destinations at the bottom of a phone screen are the Material 3 NavigationBar with NavigationBarItem, in the theme's accent colors. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For the top-level areas of an app that people switch between constantly. Use NavigationSuiteScaffold to get the bar on a phone and a navigation rail on a tablet from the same destinations.
whenNotToUse: For more than five destinations use a navigation drawer. For switching views inside one screen use tabs (PrimaryTabRow) or a segmented button.
api: @Composable fun NavigationBar(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, containerColor: Color = ..., contentColor: Color = ..., tonalElevation: Dp = ..., windowInsets: WindowInsets = ..., content: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun RowScope.NavigationBarItem(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, label: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, alwaysShowLabel: Boolean = true, colors: NavigationBarItemColors = ..., interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
@Composable fun BadgedBox(badge: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)
@Composable fun NavigationSuiteScaffold(navigationSuiteItems: NavigationSuiteScope.() -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, ..., content: @Composable () -> Unit)

states.name: selected
states.description: The item's indicator is filled and its icon and label use the selected colors.

states.name: badge
states.description: A Badge in a BadgedBox around the icon shows a count or a dot.

appearance: The bar uses the Material 3 surface and indicator colors that MonarchTheme maps from the Monarch roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes; the selected item uses the accent.
platformNotes: The web BottomTabBar draws its own bar of links with an active icon, a badge with badgeLabel, safe-area padding, a fixed position and hideFrom. On Android the bar, its window insets, the selected indicator and the badge are Material 3; items are selectable elements that call back, not links, and the app navigates. hideFrom is NavigationSuiteScaffold, which swaps the bar for a rail on wider windows. Monarch bundles no icons: the app passes them. iOS uses TabView.
accessibility: System behavior: each item is a selectable tab in TalkBack, read with its label and selected state, and has a 48dp touch target.
Keep alwaysShowLabel = true so the destination is never shown by its icon alone.
A badge inside BadgedBox is read with the item; give a count badge a content description such as "3 unread" on the item.
edgeCases: Each item is a fifth or less of the width; keep labels to one short word so they fit at font scale 2.0.
With fewer than three destinations use tabs instead.

examples.template:
NavigationBar {
        NavigationBarItem(
            selected = selected == {{items.0.key}},
            colors = NavigationBarItemDefaults.colors(indicatorColor = MonarchTheme.colors.accentSolid.copy(alpha = 0.3f)),
            onClick = { selected = {{items.0.key}} },
            icon = { MonarchIcon(imageVector = SampleIcons.Home, contentDescription = null) },
            label = { Text({{items.0.label}}) },
        )
        NavigationBarItem(
            selected = selected == {{items.1.key}},
            colors = NavigationBarItemDefaults.colors(indicatorColor = MonarchTheme.colors.accentSolid.copy(alpha = 0.3f)),

            icon = { BadgedBox(badge = { MonarchBadge(text = {{items.1.badge}}.toString(), tone = MonarchTone.Danger, variant = MonarchBadgeVariant.Solid) }) {
